sources.source_owner: DrivenData competition site / DOE GEMS Prize
observations: The competition describes predictions of geological faults indicative of geothermal resources.
The site shows an end date of 2026-12-03 at 11:59 p.m. UTC.
The same submission is scored in the initial private test round and again after expert review against an expanded label set.
External data are encouraged only when the competitor has the necessary license and can share data for independent verification.
sources.caveat: Public page content is not a private submission receipt or a participant-specific quota display.

observations: The task is to predict geological faults; the expert test faults are described as not contained in the existing public USGS fault database.
The official metric is distance-weighted Tversky with alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, and a 300 m linear triangular kernel (three 100 m pixels).
The submission must be a GeoTIFF for the full study area, UTM zone 11N / EPSG:32611, 100 m resolution, same bounds as the training data, one float32 raster layer, values in [0,1].
The official text says data outside the bounds must be null or NaN; finite zero outside is not the stated null/NaN encoding.
The problem page describes training features from USGS and INGENIOUS, and references the 1 m DEM URL list.
sources.caveat: This page verifies the written format requirements, not portal acceptance of any saved file.

sources.source_owner: National Laboratory of the Rockies / DOE GEMS Prize Official Rules
sources.status: verified PDF retrieved and parsed through sections 1.2, 3.2, 3.4, 3.5, and Appendix A
observations: Sections 3.2 and 3.4 state a limit of three submissions per week per participating entity.
Section 3.4 says each entity must select only one final submission; multiple finalized submissions are not allowed.
Section 3.5 says the chosen final submission is used across both prize rounds.
The rules require disclosure in the narrative of whether and how generative AI was used.
Appendix A.1 gives a 5:00 p.m. ET submission-time instruction on the deadline date.
sources.irregularity: The public competition homepage lists 2026-12-03 11:59 p.m. UTC, while the September 2026 official rules Appendix A.1 says 5:00 p.m. ET on the deadline date. On 2026-12-03, 5:00 p.m. ET is 22:00 UTC, earlier than 23:59 UTC. Treat the effective deadline as unresolved and use the earlier time for safety unless the organizer confirms otherwise.
sources.caveat: No participant-specific live quota, final-selection status, or portal receipt was visible without login.

sources.source_owner: U.S. Geological Survey data release; DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ
observations: USGS describes airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys over northern/western Nevada and eastern California and identifies magnetic data with subsurface structure/geology and radiometric data with surface geology/soil composition.
The page reports surveys from 2021-11-01 through 2022-11-20 and lists line, tie-line, flight-path, grid, and line-data products.
It warns that actual terrain clearance can vary in steep terrain.
The page states magnetic processing includes tie-line leveling and micro-leveling, and radiometric processing includes altitude-variation corrections.
The page marks the work CC0 1.0 Universal.
sources.caveat: The published source confirms products exist, but no new source files were downloaded or AOI-matched during this review.

sources.caveat: Catalog verification is not a download or provenance check of the repository mirror.

sources.source_owner: U.S. DOE Geothermal Data Repository, INGENIOUS Great Basin Regional Dataset Compilation; DOI 10.15121/1881483
observations: The page marks the collection publicly accessible under CC BY 4.0.
It lists data on 2 m temperature probes, faults/volcanic features, geodetic strain, heat flow, conductivity, magnetics, gravity, paleogeothermal features, seismicity, springs/wells, and geochemistry.
The page describes the files as provided as-is and assigns users responsibility for fitness for purpose.
sources.caveat: The page verifies the source and license statement; exact local files, attribution, processing, AOI coverage, and sampling bias were not rechecked.

observations: USGS describes 3DEP's mission as current high-quality topographic data and 3D representations.
The page links to 1 m DEM products, spatial metadata for current lidar availability, and elevation access tools.
The page states 3DEP products are available free of charge and without use restrictions.
sources.caveat: This program page does not establish exact usable DEM coverage/resolution for every proposed AOI cell; the coverage grid must be checked before use.

observations: Collection 2 includes Level-1 data for Landsats 1-9 and Level-2/Level-3 science products for Landsats 4-9.
The page describes global Level-2 surface reflectance and surface-temperature products from 1982 to present and U.S. Analysis Ready Data from 1982 to present.
The page notes improved geolocation and other processing updates.
sources.caveat: No scene search, cloud-free AOI check, downloaded imagery, index validation, or scene-specific license review was completed.
